title: 53rd sitting of the 20th Majlis
presiding: Speaker Abdul Raheem Abdulla; Deputy Speaker Ahmed Nazim took the chair after the 10:27-11:01 break (he also spoke once in the earlier debate as the Dhiggaru member)
summary: The sitting opened at 09:00 with routine business: a nominee for the National Integrity Commission and a nominee for ambassador to Thailand were sent to committees, and a government Sports Act amendment bill had its first reading. Most of the part was debate on Independent Institutions Committee reports: bills changing how heads of the Anti-Corruption Commission and Elections Commission are appointed, and reports recommending removal of three Elections Commission members and two Anti-Corruption Commission members, while finding no grounds to remove the Civil Service Commission chair. Government-side members supported the changes, while MDP members said they give the President too much influence over independent bodies, and the chair twice steered debate back to the report under discussion. After a break the 2025 state budget committee report was presented and its debate began; no votes were taken in this part because voting was set for the day's voting time. Seven members continued the debate on the budget committee's report on the 2025 state budget (agenda 7.6). Six spoke in favour or said they would vote for it, while the Minority Leader criticised the government's record and the budget. The sitting paused from 11:54 to 13:01 for midday prayers, then the Majlis held nine votes: it confirmed three senior Majlis staff appointments, passed amendments to the Anti-Corruption Commission and Elections Commission acts, approved dismissing two Elections Commission members, and rejected dismissing a third Elections Commission member and the Civil Service Commission president.

speakers.name: Hussain Riza Adam
positions: As committee rapporteur, presented the reports on the Anti-Corruption Commission and Elections Commission Act bills.
Presented the committee reports on removing Elections Commission members, the Civil Service Commission chair, and Anti-Corruption Commission members.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Raised a point of order on a remark that included the current government's first year, and said party action might follow for speaking.
Said he is concerned that the President appoints commission heads, since many complaints at the commission concern the President.
Pointed to the Noomadhee case as an example of complaints that were not acted on.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Raised concern over the fast-tracked removal of the Anti-Corruption Commission vice chair and a member, saying the timing raised doubts about intent.
Said the government's large majority lets it pass such changes, and questioned removing members before their terms end.
Said the report debate repeats the earlier budget debate and that committee recommendations are not binding on the government.
Criticised government borrowing and said projects promised last year, such as the Hithadhoo harbour and bridge surveys, were not delivered.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Said the Anti-Corruption Commission has produced few results over five years despite spending, and its investigative process needs fixing.
Cited cases that failed to be proven in court as showing the need to improve how cases are investigated.
Described the 2025 budget as having the smallest deficit since 2019 and directing record sums to capital investment.
Said recurrent spending has run above 70% of the budget in recent years and that the budget aims to raise revenue.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Backed the Anti-Corruption Commission amendment, saying the commission should have been replaced long ago given its record.
On the removal report, called the committee's work thorough and said the members should face legal action, not only removal.
As a budget committee member, said the committee gathered information thoroughly and the budget follows advice from international financial bodies.
Listed sector allocations, including MVR 8,251 million for health and 6,162 million for education, plus MVR 12.4 billion for public sector investment.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ismail
positions: Said independent institutions have not examined wasteful spending of state money over many years.
Said opposition members spoke about matters other than the bill, and that the President wants the commission to act on corruption.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Raised a point of order that the Kendhoo member's remarks about the President went against the Majlis rules of procedure.

speakers.name: Husnee Mubarik
positions: Said the amendment removes commission members' power to pick their own president and aligns all commissions, and that the Noomadhee case had been investigated and sent to prosecutors earlier.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Supported the Elections Commission Act amendment, saying commission heads would be set with the Majlis's approval, which he called democratic.
Said serving members would stay until their terms end, so it is not an immediate change.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Said members of independent institutions keep changing after each change of government, which he said undermines their independence.
Argued that presidential appointment of commission heads gives the President influence over bodies that oversee the government.

speakers.name: Ali Fazad
positions: Presented the 2025 budget report: spending of MVR 56.6 billion, a projected budget deficit of 7.8 percent of GDP and a primary deficit of 3.2 percent.
Said the committee reviewed fiscal policy, debt and investment plans, and passed its recommendations with the agreement of all attending members.

speakers.name: Abdul Sattar Mohamed
positions: Supported the budget and urged a quick vote, calling it an implementation budget rather than one of big new projects.
Listed planned hospitals for mental health, cancer and women and children, plus extra hospitals in Vilimale and Hulhumale.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Said the committee's report reflects thorough work and that the budget puts MVR 12.4 billion into public sector investment.
Said earlier MDP-led governments did not deliver results, and described the 2025 deficit as the smallest in a budget.
Said the budget supports housing, health, education, reclamation and water and sewerage works.

speakers.name: Abdulla Shareef
positions: Said the budget was built in line with guidance from international financial institutions to put the economy on a sustainable footing.
Criticised the previous government's spending and small pre-election budget items, saying this budget funds projects more fully.
Expected improvements in health and education and hoped the budget would pass.

speakers.name: Abdul Rahman
positions: Said he will vote for the budget although, by his count, about 68% of his constituents opposed it.
Listed Addu pledges, including the Shangri-La resort, the Hithadhoo-Hulhumeedhoo bridge and hospital upgrades, and said he would judge delivery by 2028.
Raised local concerns about roads, electricity, fishermen and tourism investment loans.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shahid
positions: Thanked the budget committee and said claims made about the budget were untrue, calling it a budget to deliver development projects.
Said the budget funds the largest projects proposed for an atoll outside Malé, welcomed Addu, and asked MDP members to help pass it quickly.
Said MDP leaders were invited to the committee looking into Israeli passport entry, and an order to attend could follow if they did not respond.

decisions: National Integrity Commission nominee sent to the Independent Institutions Committee.
Ambassador-to-Thailand nominee sent to the Foreign Relations Committee.
Sports Act amendment bill had its first reading and goes on to the next stage.
Debate on the Anti-Corruption Commission Act and Elections Commission Act amendment reports closed; votes set for the day's voting time.
Debate on the Elections Commission and Anti-Corruption Commission member-removal reports closed; votes set for the day's voting time.
Civil Service Commission chair removal report closed without debate; vote set for the day's voting time.
Appointments of the Secretary General, Counsel General and Sergeant-at-Arms to be voted on at the day's voting time.
The chair paused the sitting for midday prayers at 11:54; it resumed at 13:01.
The chair announced that the Anti-Corruption Commission's vice president and one member had resigned, so no dismissal vote on them was needed.
Fathimath Niusha was confirmed as Secretary General of the People's Majlis (79 yes, 0 no).
Fathimath Filza was confirmed as Counsel General of the People's Majlis (80 yes, 0 no).
Major (Retired) Tholhath Hassan was confirmed as Serjeant at Arms of the People's Majlis (80 yes, 0 no).
The bill amending the Anti-Corruption Commission Act (No. 13/2008), sponsored by Adam Zahir (Felidhoo), passed 69-10.
The bill amending the Elections Commission Act (No. 8/2008), sponsored by Abdulla Shareef (Kelaa), passed 69-10.
The Majlis approved removing Elections Commission vice president Ali Nashath (69-10) and member Mohamed Asif (68-10).
Removal of Elections Commission member Dr. Mohamed Zahir was not approved (0 yes, 70 no; 36 needed).
Removal of Civil Service Commission president Mohamed Nisha was not approved (12 yes, 64 no, 2 abstain; 39 needed).
